qa.answer: After this effect activates, the current timing makes a transition to the end of attack timing. For example, if this effect activates during the attack declaration timing, it will make a transition to the end of attack timing. A transition to the counter timing or block timing won't occur, and the attack won't succeed.

qa.question: Can an "end the attack" effect end an attack by a Digimon that isn't affected by effects?
qa.answer:
Yes, such attacks can be ended.
"End the attack" effects are effects that change the timing, they don't affect an attacking Digimon.

qa.question: If a Digimon's attack is ended by an "end the attack" effect, can [Counter] effects activate?
qa.answer:
No, they can't.
If an effect that ends the attack activates, the end of attack timing comes immediately. A transition to the counter timing won't occur, therefore a [Counter] effect can't be activated.

qa.question: Do [End of Attack] effects activate if I activate this card's inherited effect and end the attack from an opponent's Digimon?
qa.answer: Yes, it activates.

qa.question: Which player gains <Recovery +1 ≪Deck≫> for this card's [On Play] [When Digivolving] effect?
qa.answer: The player that activated this effect.

qa.question: What happens if this card's [On Play] [When Digivolving] effect is activated when my opponent only has a Digimon with a "this Digimon isn't affected by your opponent’s effects" effect in their battle area?
qa.answer: It can be chosen as a target for the effect, but the "if this effect didn't delete" effect will activate without your opponent's Digimon being deleted.

qa.question: What does this card's "when [...] would leave the battle area" mean, exactly?
qa.answer: "When [...] would leave the battle area" refers to when this Digimon is placed in the trash, returned to the hand/deck, placed in the security stack, moved to the breeding area, or placed under another card.

qa.question: When this Digimon would leave the battle area, can I use this card's [All Turns] effect to return 1 [Lucemon] from its digivolution cards or my trash to the bottom of the deck, but choose to not play 1 [Lucemon: Satan Mode] or 1 level 6 [Seven Great Demon Lords] trait Digimon card from my trash?
qa.answer:
Yes, you can.
This effect reads "you may play," so if you perform the conditions specified for "by X," you may choose whether or not to activate the effect shown in text.

qa.question: What does this card's "when [...] would leave the battle area other than by battle" mean, exactly?
qa.answer: "When [...] would leave the battle area other than by battle" refers to when this Digimon is placed in the trash other than as a result of a battle, returned to the hand/deck, placed in the security stack, moved to the breeding area, or placed under another card.

qa.question: Can I use this card's [All Turns] effect to place this Digimon itself as the bottom digivolution card of my [Gate of Deadly Sins] in the breeding area?
qa.answer:
No, you can't.
This Digimon hasn't yet been sent to the trash because this effect activates when this Digimon would leave the battle area, so you can't choose it from the trash as the card to place as the bottom digivolution card.

qa.question: What happens if this card's [On Play] [When Digivolving] effect is given to a Digimon that activated a "this Digimon isn't affected by your opponent’s effects until the end of your opponent's turn" effect?
qa.answer:
A Digimon with a "this Digimon isn't affected by your opponent’s effects" effect can also be chosen as a target for this effect, therefore your opponent's Digimon will be affected by this card's effect as soon as it loses the "this Digimon isn't affected by your opponent’s effects" effect.
As a result, it's deleted at the [End of Your Turn] timing.

qa.question: What does this card's "when [...] would leave the battle area other than by [...] a battle" mean, exactly?
qa.answer: "When [...] would leave the battle area other than by battle" refers to when this Digimon is placed in the trash other than as a result of a battle, returned to the hand/deck, placed in the security stack, moved to the breeding area, or placed under another card.

qa.question: Can I use this card's [All Turns] effect to delete an opponent's level 5 or lower Digimon and prevent this card from leaving the battle area?
qa.answer: Yes, you can.

qa.question: If this card's [On Play] [When Digivolving] effect deletes an opponent's Digimon with no level (such as a "Lv.-" Digimon), can I use this effect to trash cards from my deck?
qa.answer: If the card deleted has no level, you can't trash any cards.

qa.question: What does this card's "when [...] would leave the battle area other than by [...] a battle" mean, exactly?
qa.answer: "When [...] would leave the battle area other than by battle" refers to when this Digimon is placed in the trash other than as a result of a battle, returned to the hand/deck, placed in the security stack, moved to the breeding area, or placed under another card.

qa.question: Can I use this card's [All Turns] effect to place this Digimon itself as the bottom digivolution card of my [Gate of Deadly Sins] in the breeding area?
qa.answer:
No, you can't.
This Digimon hasn't yet been sent to the trash because this effect activates when this Digimon would leave the battle area, so you can't choose it from the trash as the card to place as the bottom digivolution card.

qa.question: I tried to delete my opponent's EX6-059 [Barbamon] using this card's [Main] effect. In response, my opponent uses <Scapegoat> on EX6-059 [Barbamon] to delete their other Digimon and prevent EX6-059 [Barbamon] from being deleted. At such times, is this card's "if this effect deleted" condition met?
qa.answer:
No, it isn't met.
The "if this effect deleted" condition is only met when a Digimon is deleted by this card's effect.
In this case, EX6-059 [Barbamon] wasn't deleted by this card's effect, therefore the "if this effect deleted" condition isn't met.

qa.question: Can I use this card's [All Turns] effect to play a purple Tamer card from my trash?
qa.answer: Yes, that's correct.

qa.question: What does "for each card in your opponent's hand, reduce this effect's play cost maximum by 1" in this card's [All Turns] effect mean, exactly?
qa.answer:
It means that you reduce the maximum for the play cost of the card that can be played by this effect by 1 for each card in your opponent's hand.
For example, if your opponent has 4 cards in their hand, you would reduce 10 by 4, resulting in a maximum play cost of 6, meaning that you can play 1 purple card with a play cost of 6 or less without paying the cost.

qa.question: What does this card's "when [...] would leave the battle area other than by [...] a battle" mean, exactly?
qa.answer: "When [...] would leave the battle area other than by battle" refers to when this Digimon is placed in the trash other than as a result of a battle, returned to the hand/deck, placed in the security stack, moved to the breeding area, or placed under another card.

qa.question: Can I use this card's [All Turns] effect to place this Digimon itself as the bottom digivolution card of my [Gate of Deadly Sins] in the breeding area?
qa.answer:
No, you can't.
This Digimon hasn't yet been sent to the trash because this effect activates when this Digimon would leave the battle area, so you can't choose it from the trash as the card to place as the bottom digivolution card.

qa.question: Does this card's 1st [All Turns] effect trigger when this card itself is played?
qa.answer: Yes, it triggers and activates.

qa.question: What does this card's "when [...] would leave the battle area other than by [...] a battle" mean, exactly?
qa.answer: "When [...] would leave the battle area other than by battle" refers to when this Digimon is placed in the trash other than as a result of a battle, returned to the hand/deck, placed in the security stack, moved to the breeding area, or placed under another card.

qa.question: Can I use this card's 2nd [All Turns] effect to place this Digimon itself as the bottom digivolution card of my [Gate of Deadly Sins] in the breeding area?
qa.answer:
No, you can't.
This Digimon hasn't yet been sent to the trash because this effect activates when this Digimon would leave the battle area, so you can't choose it from the trash as the card to place as the bottom digivolution card.

qa.question: When DNA digivolving into this card, can I DNA digivolve using a level 6 yellow Digimon and a level 6 black Digimon, or using a level 6 green Digimon and a level 6 purple Digimon?
qa.answer:
No, you can't.
This card's DNA digivolution can only be performed using a combination of 1 level 6 yellow or black Digimon and 1 level 6 green or purple Digimon.

qa.question: Can I use this card's <Partition (yellow/black Lv.6 & green/purple Lv.6)> effect to play a level 6 yellow Digimon and a level 6 black Digimon or a level 6 green Digimon and a level 6 purple Digimon from digivolution cards?
qa.answer:
No, you can't.
This card's <Partition (yellow/black Lv.6 & green/purple Lv.6)> effect can only play a combination of 1 level 6 yellow or black Digimon and 1 level 6 green or purple Digimon.

qa.question: Can I process the part of the effect after "then" in this card's [When Digivolving] effect even if the "if" condition in the 1st process isn't met?
qa.answer:
Yes, you can process it.
Even if this Digimon didn't DNA digivolve, this card's [When Digivolving] effect will return 1 of your opponent's Digimon to the bottom of the deck for each of this card's level 6 digivolution cards.

qa.question: Does this card's [Your Turn] effect reference the card for the Digimon before or after it digivolves?
qa.answer: It references the Digimon after it digivolves.

qa.question: Can I use this card's [Your Turn] effect to digivolve into a Digimon card with the [Beastkin], [Holy Beast] or [Cherub] trait in the hand regardless of its digivolution requirements?
qa.answer:
No, you can't.
You can’t ignore digivolution requirements when using this card's [Your Turn] effect.

qa.question: Can I use this card's [Your Turn] effect to digivolve a Digimon other than my Digimon that was suspended by an effect?
qa.answer: Yes, that's correct.

qa.question: What does this card's "when [...] would leave the battle area" mean, exactly?
qa.answer: "When [...] would leave the battle area" refers to when this Digimon is placed in the trash, returned to the hand/deck, placed in the security stack, moved to the breeding area, or placed under another card.

qa.question: If I use this card's <Delay> effect to play a Digimon from digivolution cards when my Digimon with the[Legend-Arms] trait and [EX6-042 RaijiLudomon] in its digivolution cards would be deleted, can I then use [EX6-042 RaijiLudomon]'s inherited effect to prevent the deletion?
qa.answer: Yes, you can.

qa.question: Does "the placed card" in this card's [Main] effect refer to the Digimon card with [Aqua] or [Sea Animal] in one of its traits placed from my hand as the bottom digivolution card, or does it refer to my blue Digimon?
qa.answer: It refers to the Digimon card placed from the hand as the bottom digivolution card.

qa.question: Can I use this card to place this card in the battle area without placing 1 Digimon card with the [Angel], [Archangel] or [Three Great Angels] trait from the hand at the bottom of my security stack?
qa.answer: Yes, that's correct.

qa.question: Can I use this card to place this card in the battle area without placing 1 [Seven Great Demon Lords] trait Digimon card from my hand or trash as the bottom digivolution card of my [Gate of Deadly Sins] in the breeding area?
qa.answer: Yes, that's correct.

qa.question: What happens if this card's [Main] effect is given to a Digimon that activated a "this Digimon isn't affected by your opponent’s effects until the end of your opponent's turn" effect?
qa.answer:
A Digimon with a "this Digimon isn't affected by your opponent’s effects" effect can also be chosen as a target for this effect, therefore your opponent's Digimon will be affected by this card's effect as soon as it loses the "this Digimon isn't affected by your opponent’s effects" effect.
As a result, it's deleted at the [End of Your Turn] timing.

qa.question: If this Digimon is targeted by [EX6-070 Phantom Pain]'s [End of Your Turn] effect and then this Digimon is moved to the breeding area, does [EX6-070 Phantom Pain]'s [End of Your Turn] effect activate?
qa.answer:
No, it doesn’t activate.
At the end of your turn, this card's [End of Your Turn] effect and the effect given by [EX6-070 Phantom Pain] will trigger simultaneously, then if this card's effect activates first and this Digimon is moved to the breeding area, [EX6-070 Phantom Pain]'s [End of Your Turn] effect will be pending activation, but it can't activate in the breeding area.

qa.question: Can I process the part of the effect after "then" in this card's [Main] effect even if the "if" condition in the 1st process isn't met?
qa.answer:
Yes, you can process it.
Even if your opponent doesn't have 5 or more cards in their hand, this card's [Main] effect will delete 1 of their Digimon with a level equal to or higher than the number of cards in their hand.

qa.question: Can I use this card's [Main] effect to DNA digivolve using 1 of my Digimon that isn't specified for DNA digivolution and a card in the hand?
qa.answer:
No, you can't.
You can’t ignore the requirements specified for DNA digivolution when using this card's [Main] effect.

qa.question: Can I reference [Beelzemon] and [Beelzemon (X Antibody)] as "cards with different names"?
qa.answer: Yes, you can.

qa.question: Can I reference [Beelzemon] and [Beelzemon ACE] as "cards with different names"?
qa.answer:
No, you can't.
ACE isn't included in the card name.

qa.question: I activated this card's [When Digivolving] [When Attacking] effect and placed 2 cards in this card's digivolution cards. If I activate this effect again during the same turn and place 2 more cards in this card's digivolution cards, is the "if 4 or more were placed" condition met?
qa.answer:
No, it isn't met.
This condition is only met if 4 or more cards were placed for a single activation.

qa.question: Can I return just 1 digivolution card to the bottom of the deck for the conditions of this card's [When Attacking] effect?
qa.answer:
No, you can't.
A "by" condition can't be met if only some of the required actions are performed.
You must return the specified number of digivolution cards to the bottom of the deck for the conditions of this card's [When Attacking] effect.

qa.question: I attempted to delete just 1 of my opponent's Digimon or Tamers using this card's [When Attacking] effect, but another effect prevented that Digimon or Tamer from being deleted. Is the number of cards to trash from the security stack still 7 for the part of the effect after "then"?
qa.answer: Yes, it remains 7.

qa.question: I activated this card's [When Attacking] effect, and when my opponent's Digimon would leave the battle area for the 1st process, an immediate-type effect such as a "when [...] would leave" effect caused this card to be removed from the battle area. Can I then process the part of the effect after "then" in this card's effect?
qa.answer:
Yes, you can.
If an effect activates, it is to be fully resolved even if the card that activated the effect is removed from that area during the processing.

qa.question: Can I use this card's [Your Turn] effect to digivolve into [Angewomon] or [LadyDevimon] in the trash regardless of its digivolution requirements?
qa.answer:
No, you can't.
You can’t ignore digivolution requirements when using this card's [Your Turn] effect.

qa.question: I activated this card's [Your Turn] effect when I played [ST10-04 Gatomon]. At such times, I want to digivolve [ST10-04 Gatomon] into [Angewomon] or [LadyDevimon] with the cost reduced by 1, but can I use [ST10-04 Gatomon]'s [Your Turn] effect to reduce the digivolution cost again by 2?
qa.answer: Yes, that's correct.

qa.question: Can I use this card's [End of Your Turn] effect to DNA digivolve into a Digimon card in the hand that doesn't have [DNA Digivolution]?
qa.answer: No. You can’t ignore the digivolution requirements, so you can’t DNA digivolve into a Digimon card that doesn’t have [DNA Digivolution].

qa.question: Can I use this card's [End of Your Turn] effect to DNA digivolve using Digimon cards in the hand that aren't specified in [DNA Digivolution]?
qa.answer: No. You can’t ignore the digivolution requirements, so you can’t DNA digivolve using Digimon that aren’t specified in [DNA Digivolution].

comprehensive-0223.title: <Blocker>
comprehensive-0223.text:
16-5. <Blocker>
16-5-1. <Blocker> is a keyword effect that applies a rule that allows a Digimon with that effect to block. (For details, refer to 12 "Blocking")
16-5-2. <Blocker> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")
16-5-3. Even if 1 Digimon has multiple instances of <Blocker>, the number of blocks that can be performed during the block timing is only 1.

comprehensive-0224.title: <Recovery>
comprehensive-0224.text:
16-6. <Recovery>
16-6-1. <Recovery> is a keyword effect where the specified number of cards from the specified area are placed face down on top of the security stack. This is shown on cards using text such as <Recovery +1>.
16-6-2. <Recovery> effects execute processing.

comprehensive-0225.title: <Piercing>
comprehensive-0225.text:
16-7. <Piercing>
16-7-1. <Piercing> is a keyword effect that reads "When this Digimon deletes your opponent's Digimon in battle while attacking, it checks security before the attack ends." (For details, refer to 13 "Security Checks")
16-7-2. <Piercing> is a trigger-type effect that triggers and activates when a Digimon with this effect battles an opponent's Digimon and the opponent's Digimon is deleted in battle. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger- Type Effects")
16-7-3. The security check from using <Piercing> is mandatory.
16-7-4. <Piercing> is pending processing that is processed immediately before the transition to the end of attack timing. Therefore, it will trigger simultaneously with effects triggered by the battle, but it is processed before the end of the attack. (Example: If a Digimon with <Piercing> attacks and deletes a Digimon with an [On Deletion] effect in the battle, first the [On Deletion] effect is resolved, then <Piercing> is processed.)
16-7-5. Only 1 security check can be performed during a single attack, even if <Piercing> activates multiple times. However, if the number of cards that can be checked by the attacking Digimon is modified, that number of cards will be checked in a single security check.
16-7-6. If there are no Digimon to perform a security check at the point when <Piercing> is processed, a security check won't be possible.

comprehensive-0226.title: <Draw>
comprehensive-0226.text:
16-8. <Draw>
16-8-1. <Draw> is a keyword effect where a player draws the cards from their deck according to the number specified in the effect. This is shown on cards using text such as <Draw 1>.
16-8-2. <Draw> effects execute processing.
16-8-3. A draw from <Draw> is mandatory.

comprehensive-0227.title: <Jamming>
comprehensive-0227.text:
16-9. <Jamming>
16-9-1. <Jamming> is a keyword effect where a Digimon with this effect isn't deleted as a result of a battle with an opponent's Security Digimon.
16-9-2. <Jamming> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")

comprehensive-0229.title: <Reboot>
comprehensive-0229.text:
16-11. <Reboot>
16-11-1. <Reboot> is a keyword effect where a Digimon with this effect is unsuspended during the opponent's unsuspend phase.
16-11-2. <Reboot> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")
16-11-3. Even if 1 Digimon has multiple instances of <Reboot>, it is only unsuspended once during the opponent's unsuspend phase.
16-11-4. The unsuspending from <Reboot> is mandatory.
16-11-5. The unsuspending from <Reboot> is performed at the same time as the unsuspending of the turn player's Digimon. The unsuspends aren't performed in any particular order.

comprehensive-0231.title: <Retaliation>
comprehensive-0231.text:
16-13. <Retaliation>
16-13-1. <Retaliation> is a keyword effect where a battled opponent's Digimon is deleted when a Digimon with this effect is deleted in battle.
16-13-2. <Retaliation> is a trigger-type effect that triggers when just the Digimon with this effect is deleted in battle. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger-Type Effects")
16-13-3. The processing from <Retaliation> is mandatory.

comprehensive-0233.title: <Rush>
comprehensive-0233.text:
16-15. <Rush>
16-15-1. <Rush> is a keyword effect where the Digimon with this effect can also attack in the same turn it was played.
16-15-2. <Rush> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")

comprehensive-0235.title: <Delay>
comprehensive-0235.text:
16-17. <Delay>
16-17-1. <Delay> is a keyword effect. While a card with this effect is in the battle area, by trashing that card, the effect specified in <Delay> will activate.
16-17-2. The processing from <Delay> is optional. (For details, refer to 15-7 "Optional Processing Conditions")
16-17-3. <Delay> can't be activated the same turn the card with the effect is placed in the battle area.

comprehensive-0242.title: <Raid>
comprehensive-0242.text:
16-23. <Raid>
16-23-1. <Raid> is a keyword effect that can switch the target of attack to the opponent's unsuspended Digimon with the highest DP when a Digimon with this keyword effect attacks.
16-23-2. <Raid> is a trigger-type effect that triggers when a Digimon with this effect attacks. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger-Type Effects")
16-23-3. The processing from <Raid> is optional.
16-23-4. If the opponent has multiple unsuspended Digimon with the highest DP when <Raid> activates, the player that activated the effect chooses a Digimon from among them and the attack target is switched to it.

comprehensive-0243.title: <Alliance>
comprehensive-0243.text:
16-24. <Alliance>
16-24-1. <Alliance> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with this effect attacks, by suspending 1 of your other Digimon, add the suspended Digimon's DP to the attacking Digimon and it gains <Security A. +1> for the attack.
16-24-2. <Alliance> is a trigger-type effect that triggers when a Digimon with this effect attacks. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger-Type Effects")
16-24-3. "By suspending 1 of your other Digimon" in <Alliance> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "when a Digimon with this effect attacks, by suspending 1 of your other Digimon, add the suspended Digimon's DP to the attacking Digimon and it gains <Security A. +1> for the attack" will be mandatory.
16-24-4. The value added to DP by <Alliance> is the value of the suspended Digimon upon the suspension. The added DP from <Alliance> isn't modified, even if the DP of your suspended Digimon is later modified.
16-24-5. Even if your Digimon that was suspended by <Alliance> is removed from the battle area during the attack, the added DP and <Security A. +1> remain.

comprehensive-0244.title: <Barrier>
comprehensive-0244.text:
16-25. <Barrier>
16-25-1. <Barrier> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with this effect would be deleted in battle, by trashing the top card of your security stack, this effect prevents that deletion.
16-25-2. <Barrier> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when the Digimon with this effect would be deleted in battle. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")
16-25-3. "By trashing the top card of your security stack" in <Barrier> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "prevents the deletion" will be mandatory.

comprehensive-0245.title: <Blast Digivolve>
comprehensive-0245.text:
16-26. <Blast Digivolve>
16-26-1. <Blast Digivolve> is a keyword effect that allows one of your Digimon to digivolve into a card with this keyword effect in the hand without paying the cost.
16-26-2. <Blast Digivolve> effects execute processing.
16-26-3. The processing from <Blast Digivolve> is optional.
16-26-4. <Blast Digivolve> is an effect that digivolves the chosen Digimon in the battle area.

comprehensive-0248.title: <Partition>
comprehensive-0248.text:
16-29. <Partition>
16-29-1. <Partition> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with this effect and 1 of each of the specified cards in its digivolution cards would be removed from the battle area other than by one of your effects or a battle, you may play 1 of each of the specified cards from the digivolution cards without paying their costs. This is shown on cards using text such as "<Partition (blue Lv.4 & green Lv.4)>."
16-29-2. <Partition> is an immediate-type effect that triggers "when a Digimon with this effect and 1 of each of the specified cards in its digivolution cards would be removed from the battle area other than by one of your effects or a battle." (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")
16-29-3. The processing from <Partition> is optional.
16-29-4. When <Partition> is activated, 1 of each of the specified cards is played from digivolution cards without paying their costs. A player can't choose to only play one or some of the specified cards.

comprehensive-0250.title: <Blast DNA Digivolve>
comprehensive-0250.text:
16-31. <Blast DNA Digivolve>
16-31-1. <Blast DNA Digivolve> is a keyword effect. One of your Digimon specified in this effect and a card from your hand may digivolve into a card with this keyword effect in the hand without paying the cost. This is shown on cards using text such as "<Blast DNA Digivolve> <[Durandamon] + [BryweLudramon]>."
16-31-2. <Blast DNA Digivolve> effects execute processing.
16-31-3. The processing from <Blast DNA Digivolve> is optional.
16-31-4. <Blast DNA Digivolve> is an effect that performs DNA digivolution. (For details, refer to 8-2 "DNA Digivolution")
16-31-5. A Digimon card's DNA digivolution requirements can't be ignored for <Blast DNA Digivolve>.
16-31-6. When DNA digivolution is performed using <Blast DNA Digivolve>, the player reveals the cards that will become digivolution cards from their hand at the same time as when they choose their Digimon that meet the DNA digivolution requirements.

comprehensive-0251.title: <Scapegoat>
comprehensive-0251.text:
16-32. <Scapegoat>
16-32-1. <Scapegoat> is a keyword effect. By deleting 1 of your other Digimon when a Digimon with this effect would be deleted other than by one of your effects, this effect prevents the deletion.
16-32-2. <Scapegoat> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when the Digimon with this effect would be deleted other than by one of your effects. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")
16-32-3. "By deleting 1 of your other Digimon" in <Scapegoat> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "prevents the deletion" will be mandatory.
